text.p: U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it had changed its outlook on Telefonica de Espana to negative from stable, while affirming its long-term debt rating of "AA-".

"Standard & Poor's expects Telefonica's debt coverage levels to improve to the same extent as at other telecommunications groups in the European Union. If this does not occur, the rating could be lowered. The negative outlook also reflects expectations for increased competition in telecommunications," S&P said in a statement, adding that tougher competition held true throughout Europe.
On the rating, the statement said:

"The rating reflects Telefonica's very strong market position as the primary Spanish telecommunications group as well as its adequate financial performance. Telefonica is already competing in value-added telecom services in Spain and the upcoming licensing of a second operator (Retevision) will introduce competition for basic telephony services in mid-1997. Telefonica and the second operator will operate as a duopoly until December 1998, when the market will be fully liberalised.

"While increasing competition will undoubtedly put pressure on Telefonica's margins, the company has considerably improved its competitive position over the last few years by rebalancing its tariffs and improving its infrastructure and service quality. Telefonica is also part of the Concert alliance, which further strengthens its competitive position in the Spanish and the global markets.

"On the international side, Telefonica has consolidated its position as the premier foreign telecom in Latin America, which currently contributes about 15 percent to the consolidated group's revenues and almost 20 percent to its cash-flow.

"While the Latin American operations are highly profitable and diversify the group's revenue base, they have a negative effect on the rating given the considerable entry cost and the relatively high risk profile of some of these countries.

"Consolidated finances have been gradually improving over the last few years with the funds from operations to debt ratio reaching 40 percent and the pre-tax net interest cover improving to 2.6 times in 1996. These debt coverage measures, however, remain below those of the leading European telecom operators, which together with the internaional investments explain the rating difference with the top-rated operators."
